- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is rising, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 periods ahead) when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply +1–2% bias to first 3 forecast points.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model lags in adjusting; delay forecast drop by 1–2 periods unless sentiment confirms reversal.
- If model forecast is consistently below true price over 3+ consecutive periods, apply +2–4% upward bias for next 2–3 periods to correct for mean reversion.
- For sentiment history with high volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before final output.
